title: AMD Nitro-P: VAE-Free Text-to-Image Diffusion at 90 FPS
summary: AMD's Nitro-P pixel-space diffusion model skips the VAE, hits 90 samples/s on MI300X hardware, and beats PixelDiT on GenEval benchmarks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- AMD released Nitro-P, a 679M-parameter text-to-image model that eliminates the VAE decoder and operates directly in pixel space.
- On a single Instinct MI300X, the full model scores 0.88 GenEval at 10.26 samples/s, while a one-step variant hits 90.02 samples/s.
- At 1024px resolution, Nitro-P outperforms NVLabs' PixelDiT with a 0.87 GenEval score versus 0.74, using Qwen3-1.7B for text conditioning.


AMD officially released Nitro-P on November 20, 2026, an end-to-end pixel-space[text-to-image](https://emergent.sh/glossary/image-generation)[diffusion](https://emergent.sh/glossary/diffusion-model) framework that eliminates the variational autoencoder (VAE) from the inference pipeline. Built on a 679M-parameter hierarchical E-MMDiT backbone paired with a lightweight U-Net decoder, the model achieves 0.88 GenEval at 10.26 samples per second on a single Instinct MI300X accelerator at 512×512 resolution, while a distilled one-step variant pushes throughput to 90.02 samples per second.


Published on the ROCm Blogs by AMD researchers Jingai Yu, Tong Shen, Dong Zhou, Dong Li, and Emad Barsoum, Nitro-P extends AMD's Nitro family from latent-space generation to a VAE-free pixel-space design. The authors position the framework as a departure from conventional[latent diffusion](https://emergent.sh/glossary/latent-diffusion-model) architectures that rely on separate VAE encoders and decoders for compression and reconstruction.


## Architecture and Design


Nitro-P pairs a patch-level E-MMDiT (Efficient Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformer) backbone with a lightweight U-Net for direct pixel reconstruction. By operating entirely in pixel space, the model skips the VAE decoder stage that typically adds latency and memory overhead to inference. The 679M-parameter count covers both the diffusion backbone and the reconstruction network.


Text conditioning uses Qwen3-1.7B rather than the more common Llama variants. According to the authors, Qwen3-1.7B demonstrates superior understanding of color and spatial relationships compared to Llama 3.2 1B. Training ran on 25 million text-image pairs under a progressive resolution curriculum, starting at 256×256 and scaling through 512×512 to 1024×1024.


## Benchmark Performance


At 512×512 resolution with batch size 32 on a single MI300X, the full Nitro-P model scores 0.88 on GenEval while generating 10.26 samples per second. NVLabs' PixelDiT achieves 0.78 GenEval at 5.54 samples per second under the same conditions. The one-step distilled variant trades a moderate GenEval drop to 0.85 for a throughput increase to 90.02 samples per second.


At 1024×1024 resolution, Nitro-P maintains a 0.87 GenEval score and runs at 2.44 samples per second in full mode, with the one-step version hitting 26.00 samples per second. PixelDiT scores 0.74 GenEval at the same resolution, giving Nitro-P a 0.13-point advantage. The GenEval benchmark measures compositional text-to-image alignment across attributes, relationships, and spatial reasoning.


## Release Date and Availability


Nitro-P was officially launched on November 20, 2026, through a technical post on AMD's ROCm Blogs. The release includes model weights, inference scripts, and documentation for deployment on Instinct MI300X hardware. AMD positions Nitro-P as production-ready for real-time generation workloads on its accelerator lineup.


## What This Means


Nitro-P demonstrates that pixel-space diffusion can match or exceed latent-space methods on quality benchmarks while delivering hardware-specific throughput advantages. The elimination of the VAE decoder reduces architectural complexity and memory footprint, particularly relevant for edge deployment and high-throughput serving scenarios. AMD's focus on optimizing the full stack from model architecture to silicon execution paths signals a shift toward vertically integrated AI pipelines where hardware characteristics directly inform model design choices. For practitioners evaluating text-to-image options, Nitro-P offers a viable alternative to Stable Diffusion derivatives when deploying on AMD accelerators, with the one-step variant enabling interactive generation at frame rates approaching real-time video.
